The test command now passes for both `tests` and `wsflate`.

**Cause:** `wsflate.Writer` strips the last 4 bytes of the compressed stream (the `00 00 ff ff` sync-flush tail) with `cbuf`. `Close()` then ran `checkTail()` after calling the compressor's `Close()`. Current `compress/flate` writes a final empty block (`03 00`) when closed. That pushed `ff ff 03 00` into the tail buffer. As a result, `checkTail()` failed with "unexpected stream tail". The helper's `Flush()` followed by `Close()` therefore failed in `TestWriter`, `TestHelperWriteAndRead` and `TestFlateClientServer`.

**Fix (`wsflate/writer.go`):** `Close()` now checks the tail first, while it is still the flush tail. It then redirects `cbuf` output to `ioutil.Discard` before closing the compressor. The extra final-block bytes are not part of the permessage-deflate payload, so they are dropped. Closing without a prior `Flush()` still returns an error.

My first attempt was to remove `checkTail()` from `Close()`. That produced corrupt output, so I reverted it. I wasn't able to confirm what the upstream project does here, so this fix is my own design rather than a copy of upstream.

My first run of the test command under a plain `go test` timed out after 600 s, so I didn't get its output. I reran with `-timeout 60s` and it finished in under a second. I didn't find out why the first run hung. It may have been related to my first attempted change.
